name: Pipeline parallelism for LLM inference: when PP beats TP and the bubble problem
arithmetic_intensity: PP splits a model layer-wise, where each GPU is responsible for a subset of layers. The arithmetic intensity of each stage is the same as a dense model at the same batch size, but the batch is split into micro-batches that flow through the pipeline. The key advantage over TP: PP requires only point-to-point communication (activations) once per stage, rather than a collective per layer. The key disadvantage: pipeline bubbles - if one stage is slower than the others, the entire pipeline stalls. Sarathi-Serve showed that chunked prefill with stall-free scheduling can reduce pipeline bubbles by creating balanced micro-batches, achieving up to 5.6x gains in end-to-end serving capacity for Falcon-180B with pipeline parallelism.
scales_with: num_stages (more stages = more parallelism but also more bubbles)
micro_batch_size (larger micro-batches = fewer bubbles but more memory)
batch_size (larger batches = more micro-batches = better pipeline utilization)
prompt_length (longer prompts = more variable execution time = more bubbles)
workarounds: Pipeline parallelism (PP): split model layer-wise across GPUs, avoiding per-layer all-reduce
Sarathi-Serve chunked prefill: balanced micro-batches reduce pipeline bubbles
Micro-batching: split batch into micro-batches that flow through the pipeline
Combine PP with TP: use PP across nodes and TP within nodes for large models
AlpaServe: statistical multiplexing with model parallelism for multi-model serving
notes: When PP beats TP: for deep models that don't fit on a single GPU, PP is preferred because (1) it requires only point-to-point communication (activations) once per stage, rather than a collective per layer, (2) it scales linearly with the number of GPUs, and (3) it tolerates slow fabrics better than TP. When TP beats PP: for shallow models or when high-bandwidth interconnects (NVLink) are available, TP is simpler and has lower overhead. The bubble problem is the key challenge: if one stage is slower than the others, the entire pipeline stalls. Sarathi-Serve's chunked prefill with stall-free scheduling addresses this by creating balanced micro-batches. The measured result is up to 5.6x gains in end-to-end serving capacity for Falcon-180B with pipeline parallelism. DistServe also showed that inter-op parallelism (PP) becomes advantageous as the arrival rate increases, because it reduces queuing delay.
